Quote verbatim; 'only acute toxicities ... cytopenias' and 2-day fever confirmed in full text. But no source compares model and patient before 2012, when contra overrides anyway. Delete this entry: the cell runs 2010 untested to 2012 contra.

Quote verbatim (abstract). Table 1 FL = patients 1, 2, 8 (3 of 8, patient 1 treated twice; draft says 4). Patient 8 toxicities confirmed. Neither this paper nor the FDA review compares mice with patient CRS: contra is juxtaposed, see rule_questions. Epub 2011-12-08, print 2012 correct.

missing: Context note claims 'the first CD19 CAR-T patient ever treated (2010) had FL'. Wrong: Jensen 2010 BBMT (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbmt.2010.03.014, epub 2010-03-19) reports earlier City of Hope first-generation CD19-CAR infusions in refractory FL (no overt toxicity, persistence 24 h to 7 days, no responses), and Brentjens' CLL patients were treated 2007-2009. Say 'the first reported CD19 CAR-T regression was in an FL patient'. Jensen 2010 is also an in-class FL patient result with no model comparison (a first-generation CAR that failed, which no model flagged): belongs in the efficacy strip as untested at 2010 if first-generation CARs count as the class.

File name says 'cd19-directed-depleters' but the draft covers CAR-T only. If the class includes CD19 antibodies/ADCs in FL (tafasitamab, inMIND; loncastuximab tesirine), they rest on different models (MOR208 and ADCT-402 xenografts) and need their own entries. Not researched here; scope decision for the caller.

Safety untested 2010: the mouse paper's Discussion makes an explicit prospective prediction ('The prolonged B-cell depletion is also a warning that patients enrolled on clinical trials...'); quote it as the model's stated safety prediction rather than the 143-day sentence.

Registry: NCT00924326 results first posted 2019-03-21 (ACTUAL) confirmed via CT.gov v2; its conditions list names only 'DLBCL transformed from FL', not FL itself, because the record reflects later amendments; the 2010/2012 papers establish the FL patients.
rule_questions: Safety contra 2012 rests on juxtaposition: model silence is in the primary mouse paper ('The only toxicity ever noted in the treated mice was a lack of B cells') and Yescarta review 4.3; patient CRS/neurotoxicity is in Kochenderfer 2012; no source puts them side by side (confirmed in both full texts). Rule 1 (a primary source must make the comparison) would send this to untested, but the safety question explicitly scores a model's silence and v2's comparison_stated=false exists for this case. Recommend keeping contra and stating that silence-type failures are allowed with comparison_stated=false.

The 2012 comparison sentence compares murine studies with 'these early clinical reports' (the 2010 FL case report plus CLL/ALL reports from other groups); the paper's own cohort has 3 FL patients. Is a comparison stated over mixed-histology reports sufficient for the FL context? Treated as yes because the FL case report is among them and the cohort includes FL.

Year convention: Kochenderfer 2012 epub 2011-12-08, print 2012; house rule (print year) gives 2012, so the same-status strip starts 2012 not 2011. ELARA (epub 2021, print 2022) has the same split in the judgement text.
